### `Nscriptmismatch`: candidate definitions (base: 213 v1-pipeline items with pull)

| definition | n |
|---|---|
| **adopted**: host_original contains letters of a non-Latin script, host_pipeline contains only Latin letters, and every control contains letters of a non-Latin script | 100 |
| same, at least one control in a non-Latin script | 100 |
| same, most controls in a non-Latin script | 100 |
| host_pipeline only Latin letters and every control non-Latin (host_original not checked) | 102 |
| host_original non-Latin and host_pipeline only Latin (controls not checked) | 111 |
| stored flags: host_is_romanization == 1 (host_pipeline != host_original) and controls_latin == 0 | 110 |
| first report, old letter test: host non-Latin → Latin, >= 1 control non-Latin | 98 |
| first report, old letter test: same, every control non-Latin | 97 |

Adopted because it is the reading of the sentence in section 6.2: the host was romanised (the original form is in a non-Latin script, the pipeline form is in Latin letters) and the controls are in the original script (non-Latin). The old value 99 is not used.

- Items where only some controls are non-Latin: 0. So 'all', 'most' and 'at least one' give the same count.
- Adopted items whose controls use a non-Latin script that does not occur in host_original: 0.
- Items with a non-Latin host_original and controls in Latin letters (romanised host, Latin controls; not counted): 11 (SEA_001, SEA_002, SEA_003, SEA_004, SEA_005, SEA_009, SEA_010, SEA_013, SEA_014, MET_012, EEU_010). Most are Malay/Javanese items whose host_original adds a Jawi or Javanese-script gloss.
- Items whose host_pipeline still contains non-Latin letters (not counted): SEA_011 (`khan hu (หูคัน)`).
- The first report's letter test counted modifier letters (Hawaiian ʻokina, the Arabic ʿayn sign) as non-Latin; this is corrected here, which is why the earlier 97/98 differ.

### Tradition and language labels

Strong candidates are merged (author's decision of 2026-10-23): labels that become the same name once a parenthetical, a ' — ' subtitle (traditions only), diacritics and modifier letters, case and an unambiguous ISO code (languages only) are removed. The merged name is the label with the most items (tie: the shorter one without its parenthetical, then the shorter full label, then alphabetical). Weak candidates (shared segment of a '/' list, one name contained in the other, very similar spelling) are not merged; they are listed in `results/harmonisation_weak_for_author.csv`. The author decided on 2026-10-23 not to merge weak candidates (final). `NtradLabelsMin` and `NlanguagesMin` count labels with every weak pair merged too (connected components, known false matches excluded; `results/harmonisation_all_weak_merged.csv`, sensitivity only).

| kind | labels before | labels after | labels in a merged group | labels with a weak candidate | weak pairs |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| tradition | 75 | 63 | 18 | 13 | 9 |
| language | 50 | 43 | 11 | 30 | 24 |

## (d) Manuscript checks

Written to `paper/manuscript_checks.md`, which is not tracked (the manuscript is not in the repository).

## Rules

- `int`: count, integer; {,} from 1,000
- `k2`: kappa, 2 decimals, ROUND_HALF_UP
- `icc3`: ICC, 3 decimals, ROUND_HALF_UP
- `z2`: z, 2 decimals, ROUND_HALF_UP
- `p`: p, APA: '< .001' if p < .001, else '= .xxx' (3 decimals, ROUND_HALF_UP, no leading 0)
- `pct1`: percent, 1 decimal, ROUND_HALF_UP, no % sign
- `m3`: mean pull / intercept, 3 decimals, ROUND_HALF_UP, minus sign only when negative
- `rho`: Spearman rho range min--max, 2 decimals, ROUND_HALF_UP
- `empty`: empty string if the check passes, else \missing{...}
- `mio`: parameter count in millions, integer, ROUND_HALF_UP
- `d2`: standardised effect d, 2 decimals, ROUND_HALF_UP
- `ci3`: 95% CI as [lower, upper], 3 decimals each, ROUND_HALF_UP
